children: Malaysian palm oil futures climbed more than 1% on Tuesday as trading resumed after a holiday, with firmer rival edible oil and crude oil prices supporting the market.

The benchmark palm oil contract (FCPOc3) for November delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange rose 89 ringgit, or 1.82%, to 4,983 ringgit ($1,235.25) a metric ton in early trade, extending gains to a second session.
FUNDAMENTALS
Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) rose 0.93%, while its palm oil contract
added 0.77%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (BOcv1) were up 2.28%.
Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.
Oil prices gained as the resumption of fighting between the U.S. and Iran in the Middle East renewed fears of supply disruptions from the world's key crude-producing region. O/R
Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.
The ringgit
, palm's currency of trade, weakened 0.3% against the dollar, making the commodity slightly cheaper for buyers holding foreign currencies.
Indonesia has raised the amount of diesel allocated to its subsidy programme in 2027, while keeping its liquefied petroleum gas allocation unchanged, the energy ministry said.
Indonesia has set its September crude palm oil reference price at $1,007.51 per ton, a trade ministry regulation showed.

Indonesian state-owned plantation firm Agrinas Palma Nusantara currently has 3 million hectares (11,583 square miles) of land under its control after handing over 1 million hectares to fellow state enterprise Perhutani, the company's chief executive said.
Palm oil may rise into a range of 4,949-4,990 ringgit per ton, following its stabilisation around 4,814 ringgit, Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said. TECH/C

* Selling drove global bond yields to major new highs on Tuesday as renewed fighting in the Middle East lifted oil prices above $90 a barrel and put pressure on stock markets around the world. MKTS/GLOB
